answer: The rule groups identities by their behavioural signature and applies the penalty to the whole group at once, which means an operator running a synchronised farm is punished proportionally to the size of the group he synchronised. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. The vault is the collateral at risk, the pulse the behavioural signature that groups identities, and the meadow the joint forfeiture that punishes the group: splitting into many pulse groups avoids the joint loss but scatters the vault into smaller, individually useless stakes.
